# Pool World v10.50 — isolated 180–240ms shot continuity
**Date:** 2026-10-28 UTC  
**Branch:** `development/poolworld-match-engine`  
**Production status:** BLOCKED — do not edit `main/index.html` without independent physical Samsung/human acceptance and explicit owner approval.

## Reproducible user-visible defect
After ordinary 60Hz frames, an isolated 180–240ms Android/Chromium animation gap advanced a moving cue ball by eight 120Hz physics ticks immediately, with additional stale simulation time banked for the next callback. In the unchanged 360×800 fixture at 75% power, the 180ms gap moved the cue **25.77577 table units** on the returning callback and **25.48137 more units** on the next ordinary 16.7ms frame. The selected shot impulse remained calibrated at **6.51294**, but the rendered movement visibly lurched. At 25% power the same baseline returned **10.38351 units** followed by **10.12578**.

## Mandatory reproducing regression
New `tests/test_pool60_short_gap.py`, registered in `.github/workflows/poolworld-staging-tests.yml`, covers 412 Chromium checks across 360×800, 390×844, 844×390 and 768×1024 viewports. It verifies four gaps (180/200/220/240ms), 25%/75% selected power, two warm-up lengths, zero unintended physics advancement, zero stale debt, no rendered cue jump, unchanged selected impulse/velocity, smooth next-frame recovery, sustained 5/5.5fps real-time catch-up, and genuine 28ms post-input motion for freshly fired shots. This is synthetic browser timing, **not** Samsung hardware acceptance.

Test-only commit `7e7719021d964d37d070440893be5b9f6b267acc`; workflow registration commit `6040a9bc26ad2c908a85de3f4c7a407d1e5209a5`.

- Final documented staging candidate **#591** (`40707997002`) succeeded with **412/412 new checks and 12,858/12,858 checks across 98 numerical summaries**; completed jobs and decoded logs inspected.

## Gameplay correction
On a moving shot after recent normal frame pacing, the existing isolated-hitch classifier now recognizes 180–350ms gaps (previously 250–350ms). It suppresses the single returning-frame fast-forward and clears stale simulation debt. If the next callback is also slow, the existing bounded sustained-low-FPS debt recovery repays the deferred time; if normal, it discards it. Genuine newly fired shots still receive only their actual post-input time. No changes to `shotSpeed`, cue/object collision physics, six-pocket capture, rules, or recorded audio.

Final staging gameplay blob `d2895cec8303a921cd29ef344b71920f76c03728`, commit `b04036b9f16d6ad5b808681cbae3bd00e195fb79`. Promoted the **exact passing blob** to development branch-root `index.html` in commit `11b0f69d37959de58c7d6eac5f675211d90211a4`.
